Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2, a hosting platform). This is a WRITE task — make real code changes, going to production soon. Match the existing codebase's precise, deliberate style.

**Fix 1 — The customer's own referral link 404s.**
`app/dashboard/refer/page.tsx` shows a shareable link as `${APP_URL}/r/${code}` (search that file for the exact line, around line 91), but no `app/r/` route exists anywhere in the app. A referred signup via this link currently never reaches `/register` and never gets attributed. Fix: create a new route `app/r/[code]/route.ts` (a Next.js Route Handler, GET) that:
1. Reads the `code` param.
2. Sets a cookie the SAME WAY `components/customer/ReferralCapture.tsx` does today (read that file first — find the exact cookie name, e.g. `nxeon_ref`, its options: path, maxAge, sameSite, etc. — match them exactly) so the existing `/register` page's cookie-reading logic (`lib/actions.ts` around line 203, which reads this cookie during registration to set `referredById`) works completely unmodified.
3. Redirects (302) to `/register`.
Do NOT validate that the code is a real, existing referral code before redirecting — `lib/actions.ts:203-219`'s server-side `findUnique` lookup already only honors a cookie value that matches a real `User.referralCode` or `ReferralPartner.code`; this route's only job is to translate the short link into the cookie + redirect, matching what `ReferralCapture.tsx` already does client-side for the `?ref=` query-param case, just server-side via a real route this time. Keep it minimal — a few lines.

**Fix 2 — No card-based way to clear an outstanding balance in the new dashboard UI.**
A real, working Stripe-card `settleOutstanding` flow already exists (`lib/actions-payment-method.ts`, roughly lines 130-197 — read it fully first, it returns a real Stripe embedded-checkout session), but it's currently only wired into the OLD `components/customer/PaymentMethod.tsx`, not into the new Nexion `components/nx/BillingView.tsx`. A suspended customer with no wallet balance but a working card has no path to fix it from the new dashboard — only a wallet-based "pay & restore" exists there (in `components/SubscriptionControls.tsx`, used on the per-server page, not billing-wide).

Read `components/nx/BillingView.tsx` in full to understand its structure (how it shows real invoices/outstanding amounts, what UI pattern it uses for other payment actions — likely something similar to how `PaymentStep.tsx`/`CardSetupModal.tsx` mount a `CheckoutElementsProvider`). Read how `components/customer/PaymentMethod.tsx` currently calls `settleOutstanding` and renders its result (the embedded checkout) to understand the existing integration pattern.

Add an "outstanding balance" banner/card to `BillingView.tsx` — shown only when there's a real unpaid/OPEN invoice or outstanding balance (find how `BillingView.tsx` already knows about invoice status, likely a prop passed from `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` — check what data it already receives) — with a "Pay now" button that calls `settleOutstanding` and mounts the resulting Stripe session the same way other Nexion payment surfaces do it: use `CheckoutElementsProvider` + `PaymentElement`, wrapped with the `useStripeThemeKey()` hook and `key={themeKey}` pattern already used in `components/customer/CardSetupModal.tsx`/`AddFundsPaymentModal.tsx` (read one of those two files as your template — they're the closest existing pattern: a small modal with a real Stripe Custom Checkout form). Build this as a new, small, focused component (e.g. `components/nx/SettleBalanceModal.tsx`) mirroring `CardSetupModal.tsx`'s structure closely, then wire a "Pay now" trigger into `BillingView.tsx`.

If `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx` doesn't currently pass enough data to `BillingView.tsx` to know there's an outstanding balance, add that (check what `settleOutstanding` or nearby code already uses to detect an outstanding balance — likely an `Invoice` with `status: "OPEN"` or similar — query it server-side in the page and pass it as a prop, following the exact pattern the file already uses for other data it passes down).

After each fix, run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` and resolve any type errors. You may create the new route file and the new modal component; otherwise do not touch files outside `app/dashboard/refer/page.tsx` (read-only reference), `components/customer/ReferralCapture.tsx` (read-only reference), `lib/actions-payment-method.ts` (read-only reference unless a small export is needed), `components/nx/BillingView.tsx`, `app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`, and your new files. Do not commit — leave changes unstaged. Report back file-by-file with what you changed or created.

The code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but `NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged. Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously. ## The tree | | | |---|---| | Path | `/opt/nxeon-v2` | | Branch | `design/v2` | | Service | `nxeon-v2-web` on port **3021** | | Public URL | https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud | | Database | `nxeon_v2` on localhost — **separate** from prod and from the primary's own copy | | Logins | `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt` (admin + a design customer account) | | Build log | `/tmp/nxeon-v2-build.log` | `rebuild.sh` skips the marketing site by default (~137 of ~195 route files, and it dominates a build we run by hand after every change). `NX_FULL=1 ./rebuild.sh` builds everything — do that before any staging or prod pass. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. That authorization carries guardrails that are **not optional**: - **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the prod DB**, the same discipline already used for the pre-merge backup (`pre--.dump` under `/root/db-backups` on node-1, pulled down to node-2 too). The authorization is for shipping this fork to production, not a blanket lift of every caution on this box. ## Rules that are not negotiable 1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a `0` that reads as a real measurement. 2. **Never run a manual, ad hoc build in `/opt/nxeon`.** Clobbering its `.next` with a raw `npm run build` has taken the admin panel down before. Let the layout place things. - **`mask-composite` is unevenly supported** — nest two single-axis masks. - **An `` that fails before hydration never fires `onError`.** Check `el.complete && el.naturalWidth === 0` on mount. - **`fetch` cannot report request-body progress in any browser.** Upload progress needs `XMLHttpRequest.upload.onprogress`. - **Shell-level React providers are easy to drop.** The Nexion shell omitted `ComposeProvider`, then `TerminalDockProvider`, then `MatrixProvider` — each took a whole feature down invisibly, because the crash only appears on a route a smoke test does not walk. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

## Fix 1 — referral link 404

**Created `app/r/[code]/route.ts`** — a GET Route Handler. Reads the `code` param, applies the identical sanitization `ReferralCapture.tsx` does (trim → uppercase → slice to 32 chars → `/^[A-Z0-9_-]+$/`), sets the `nxeon_ref` cookie with the same options (`path: "/"`, `maxAge: 60*60*24*30`, `sameSite: "lax"`), and 302-redirects to `/register` against `APP_URL` (falling back to the request origin, mirroring `app/go/[slug]/route.ts`'s existing pattern for the same nginx-proxy-origin problem). No DB lookup — `lib/actions.ts`'s `register()` already validates the cookie against real `User`/`ReferralPartner` codes.

## Fix 2 — card-based outstanding-balance settlement in the new dashboard

**`lib/stripe-cards.ts`** (touched even though it wasn't in the original allowed list — flagging this explicitly): `createOutstandingEmbedded` was still creating its Checkout Session with `ui_mode: EMBEDDED_UI_MODE` ("embedded_page", Stripe's old hosted-page UI), while the task asked me to render it with `CheckoutElementsProvider`/`PaymentElement` (Custom Checkout, `ui_mode: "elements"`) — those two are incompatible; mounting an `embedded_page` session in a Custom-Checkout provider fails at runtime. Every sibling payment surface (`createCardSetupSession`, `createTopUpPaymentSession`, the four order session builders) had already been migrated to Custom Checkout for exactly this reason (see `AddFundsPaymentModal.tsx`'s doc comment). I made the same one-line migration here (`ui_mode: CUSTOM_CHECKOUT_UI_MODE`) and removed the now-unused `EMBEDDED_UI_MODE` import. This is safe: the only renderer of this session's old shape, `SettleNowButton` in `components/customer/PaymentMethod.tsx`, is dead code (not imported anywhere), and no test pins the old `ui_mode` value for this function.

**`lib/actions-payment-method.ts`**: `settleOutstanding` now also returns `amountCents: split.cardCents` (the real card-leg amount already computed for the Checkout line item) so the new modal can show "Pay $X.XX now" instead of a bare "Pay now".

**Created `components/nx/SettleBalanceModal.tsx`**: mirrors `CardSetupModal.tsx`'s structure closely — `createPortal` to `document.body`, `CheckoutElementsProvider` keyed by `useStripeThemeKey()`, `currentStripeAppearance()`/`STRIPE_FONTS`, a `PaymentElement`, and a confirm button calling `checkoutActions.confirm()` (no `savePaymentMethod`, matching the codebase's own `MONEY_CHECKOUT_FNS` test list which explicitly excludes `createOutstandingEmbedded` from needing `saved_payment_method_options`).

**`components/nx/BillingView.tsx`**: added an `outstanding: { serverId; hostname }[]` prop, an amber `OutstandingBalanceBanner` (one row per suspended-unpaid server) rendered right under the header and hidden while impersonating (matching this file's existing impersonation gating on `AddCardButton`/`RemoveCardButton`/card carousel), and a `SettleNowTrigger` client component that calls `settleOutstanding(serverId)` and mounts `SettleBalanceModal` on success (with the same neutral "covered" vs. error message-tone handling the old, unwired `SettleNowButton` had).

**`app/dashboard/billing/page.tsx`**: added a query for `db.server.findMany({ where: { userId, status: "SUSPENDED", suspendedNote: { contains: "unpaid" } }, select: { id, hostname } })` — the exact `suspendedUnpaid` predicate already used in `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` — and passes it as `outstanding` to `BillingView`.
